newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Postal Insurance wary of JGB investment.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Postal Insurance wary of JGB investment.

text.p: The prevailing low yield on yen-denominated bonds is forcing Japan's Postal Life Insurance Bureau, a major institutional investor, to take a cautious stance toward investing in Japanese government bonds (JGBs), an official at the bureau said on Monday.
"Generally speaking, the recent fall in yen bond yields has lowered their attractiveness as an investment vehicle," said the official from the bureau's Fund Management Division.
"Therefore, we cannot avoid becoming more cautious toward JGBs," the official said.

The Postal Life Insurance Bureau, or Kampo, currently guarantees a 2.75 percent yield for new holders of its 10-year insurance policy. The bureau has guaranteed a yield of about 3.75 percent to those who bought the policy last year and the year before that.
This compares with a benchmark 182nd JGB yield of 2.630 percent on Monday.
The bureau may consider selling low-yielding yen bonds in its portfolio if the bond yield stays around recent levels, a source close to the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications said.
Kampo now holds a little under four trillion yen in foreign bonds, the source said.

"Stocks and foreign bonds are well-performing investment vehicles. So far, Kampo has been cautious about investing in foreign bonds due to the strong yen, but the time has come to reconsider this strategy," the source said.
The Kampo official said, however, that Kampo would be buying some JGBs to meet portfolio needs.
